# ARMORED FLIGHT

A complete, playable, single-player 3D action game that runs entirely in the browser: you pilot a high-tech
powered-armour suit over a destructible modern city at sunset, fighting drone swarms, rooftop missile turrets and a
giant shielded boss.

* **Vite + TypeScript + Three.js** (rendering, HUD, post-processing)
* **Rapier (`@dimforge/rapier3d-compat`, WASM)** – all collisions, raycasts, projectiles, debris and the player's flight body
* **Blender (`bpy` scripts)** – every 3D asset is generated by the scripts in `tools/blender/` and exported to `public/assets/*.glb`
* Client side only: no server, no database, no external runtime API, no downloaded models, procedural audio (WebAudio)

```
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
npm run build        # type-check + production bundle in dist/
npm run preview      # serve the production bundle
```

The generated `.glb` files are committed in `public/assets/`, so **Blender is only needed if you want to regenerate the assets**:

```
npm run assets            # rebuilds every GLB with Blender (deterministic) and validates it against tools/asset-contract.json
npm run assets:validate   # only validate the GLBs that are already in public/assets
npm run assets:info       # print the Blender / Python versions that will be used
```

`tools/run-blender.mjs` finds Blender via `$BLENDER` / `$BLENDER_PATH`, `PATH`, a portable copy unzipped into `tools/.blender/`, or the
usual install locations. Any Blender 4.4 build works (`--factory-startup`, background mode); the portable ZIP from
[blender.org/download](https://www.blender.org/download/) unzipped into `tools/.blender/` is enough (this repository was built with 4.4.3).
The individual scripts can also be run directly, e.g.

```
blender -b -P tools/blender/build_player.py
node tools/run-blender.mjs tools/blender/build_player.py -- --preview      # also renders preview PNGs to tools/.cache/previews/
```

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| `W` / `S` | thrust forward / back |
| `A` / `D` | strafe left / right |
| `Space` / `C` | vertical thrust up / down (hold `C` near a surface to land) |
| Mouse | aim (yaw / pitch) – the crosshair is where the palm repulsors converge |
| `Q` / `E` | roll (barrel roll; the suit auto-levels and banks into turns) |
| `Shift` | boost (drains energy, intensifies thrusters, widens the FOV, adds vibration and speed lines) |
| `F` | toggle hover mode / cruise flight |
| `LMB` | repulsors (alternating palms; `X` switches to dual fire) |
| `RMB` | target lock on / off (SEARCHING → ACQUIRING → LOCKED, takes ~1.2 s and can be lost) |
| `1` | fire a homing missile (needs a LOCK) |
| `2` | fire a mini-missile salvo (6 rockets, they pick nearby targets on their own) |
| `Tab` | switch target |
| `H` / `F1` | controls overlay · `M` mute · `F3` performance stats · `Esc` pause |

## How to play

* You start standing on a rooftop. Press `Space` (or any thrust key) to lift off.
* **Waves 1-2**: drone raids, on top of the missile turrets that are dug in on ~11 rooftops. **Wave 3**: the *Armored Behemoth* with escorts.
  Break its energy shield first (the dome flashes, flickers and finally dissolves), then hit the exposed core before the shield regenerates.
  After the victory you can continue into endless waves.
* **Missiles are finite** (8 missiles, 24 mini-missiles); destroyed enemies drop supply canisters (armour, energy, missiles, mini-missiles), every cleared wave resupplies you
  (a *full* resupply before the boss wave - save your missiles for the shield) and the armour slowly self-repairs while nobody is hitting you.
* The repulsors never run dry but draw on the same **energy** bar as the boost; a fraction of every hit is absorbed by the energy shield.
* When the Behemoth arrives its **jamming field switches the rooftop turrets off** - the boss wave is a duel with the boss and its escorts.
* Lost your suit? **RETRY WAVE** restarts the wave you died in (city, kills and score are kept); **RESTART MISSION** starts from scratch.
* **Difficulty** (menu / pause screen): *Easy* (40 % less damage, double armour self-repair), *Normal*, *Hard* (35 % more damage, slower repair).
  The boss has three phases of vulnerability: shield → exposed core (repulsors do extra damage to it) → enrage below 35 % hull; every broken shield shakes loose supply canisters.
* Enemy missiles can be **outmanoeuvred around buildings**, out-boosted, or **shot down** with the repulsors. The radar, off-screen arrows and the `MISSILE INBOUND` alert help.
* The city is destructible: water towers, city signs, columns and kiosks shatter into real Rapier rigid-body fragments; cars, lamps and barriers are launched by explosions.
* Ramming buildings hurts – impact damage scales with the collision speed.

## The Blender asset pipeline

All art is produced by `bpy` scripts (`tools/blender/`) – nothing is downloaded and nothing is hand-made outside the scripts:

| Script | Output (`public/assets/`) |
|---|---|
| `build_player.py` | `player.glb` – the armour (`PlayerRoot` → `Pelvis` → `Torso`, `Helmet`, `Arm/Forearm/Hand_L/R`, `PalmReactor_L/R`, `ChestReactor`, `Leg/Shin/Boot_L/R`, `FootThruster_L/R`, launcher / muzzle / nozzle empties) with three pose animations `Pose_Standing`, `Pose_Flight`, `Pose_Hover` |
| `build_enemies.py` | `drone.glb`, `turret.glb` (base / yaw / pitch assemblies), `boss.glb`, `boss_shield.glb` |
| `build_projectiles.py` | `missile.glb`, `mini_missile.glb` |
| `build_pickups.py` | `pickups.glb` |
| `build_city_buildings.py` | `city_buildings.glb` – **12** building modules (glass tower, set-back art-deco tower, office slab, apartment block with balconies, L-shaped tower, warehouse, brick residential tower, round tower, mid-rise, landmark, parking garage, podium tower) with baked facade textures (albedo / ORM / emissive / normal), authored `COL_` collision boxes, `Roof_Slot_` markers and LOD1 versions |
| `build_city_ground.py`, `build_city_props.py` | `city_ground.glb` (road, intersection, sidewalk straight / corner, plaza lot - all with generated textures), `city_props.glb` (22 props: street lamp, 3 cars, 2 barriers, antenna, AC units, vent stack, roof access, cooling tower, solar array + hydrant, bench, bus shelter, traffic light, planter, dumpster, tree, cone, trash bin) |
| `build_destructibles.py` + `fracture.py` | `destructible_{column,citysign,watertower,smallbuilding}_{intact,fractured}.glb` – the fractured states contain real irregular chunk meshes (`chunk_001…`) made by a procedural Voronoi fracture implemented in `bpy` (Blender's Cell Fracture add-on is not available in a stock build) |
| `build_all.py` | runs everything (each script in its own factory-settings Blender process) |

The whole pipeline is **deterministic**: `npm run assets` takes about a minute and rebuilding all 19 GLB files twice gives byte-identical output
(fixed seeds, no clocks, stable ordering, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, a hand-written UV sphere instead of Blender's process-dependent one).

Conventions (`tools/blender/ASSET_SPEC.md`): metres, Blender +Y forward = three.js −Z, emission axes of muzzle / nozzle / launcher empties are their local +Y,
identical palette across all assets. `tools/asset-contract.json` is the machine-readable contract that both the game (`src/assets/loader.ts`) and
`tools/validate-assets.mjs` use – it checks node names, hierarchy, animation clips, triangle budgets, dimensions and chunk counts.

## Architecture (src/)

```
core/      input (pointer lock), math, seeded RNG, typed event bus
physics/   Rapier world wrapper: collision groups, raycasts, sphere casts, contact events
assets/    GLB loader driven by the asset contract
world/     sky dome + IBL + sun rig, city layout / instancing / LODs, destructibles, props, debris, pickups
player/    6-DoF flight model, Rapier body, armour rig (pose blending + procedural arm aiming), weapons, targeting, chase camera
enemies/   finite-state-machine AI: drones, turrets, boss (+ shield), wave director
weapons/   homing missiles / mini-missiles / plasma bolts (all Rapier bodies) and the explosion handler
fx/        instanced particle system, beams, shockwaves, shield shader, post-processing (bloom, speed / boost / damage pass)
ui/        HTML/CSS HUD (radar, brackets, off-screen arrows, gauges), overlays / menus
audio/     fully procedural WebAudio sound engine
game/      Game (fixed 60 Hz simulation + interpolated rendering), shared context / types
```

Highlights: fixed-step simulation with interpolated visuals; the player's capsule collider follows the armour's pitch lean, so physics
and visuals always agree; repulsor beams start at the palm reactors and converge on the reticle; missiles leave the shoulder racks on a curved
departure arc, then home in with a finite turn rate, smoke trails and proximity fuses; every explosion applies radial damage and velocity kicks to
enemies, debris, props and destructibles; buildings are instanced per 200 m chunk with LOD1 swapping and authored `COL_` collision boxes as fixed Rapier colliders.

## Testing helpers

`tools/dev/bot.js` is a scripted autopilot used for automated playtests (not part of the shipped game). With the dev server running open
`http://localhost:5173/?nopause` and, in the console:

```js
const { bot } = await import('/tools/dev/bot.js'); bot.attach();
window.__game.start(); window.__game.state = 'playing';
bot.bossTrial(200);        // restart -> boss wave -> fight for up to 200 simulated seconds, returns a summary
window.__game.advance(5);  // run 5 s of the fixed-step simulation immediately (no rendering)
```

`tools/dev/sandbox.html` is a small viewer that loads the real game classes for looking at single assets.

## Enemy AI (finite state machines)

Every enemy is a small explicit finite state machine (`src/enemies/fsm.ts`: `enter / update / exit` per state, transitions requested with `go()`):

| Enemy | States (transitions) |
|---|---|
| **Drone** (`drone.ts`) | `patrol` (waypoints around its spawn) → `chase` (player inside aggro range, or when shot) → `attack` (circle-strafe on an orbit around the player, predictive burst fire, needs line of sight) → `evade` (a homing missile is inbound: chaff burst + dodge perpendicular to the missile) → back to `attack` / `chase`; `wreck` when destroyed (tumbles, smokes, explodes on impact). Steering uses ray-cast whiskers against the Rapier world for building avoidance. |
| **Turret** (`turret.ts`) | `dormant` (idle scan) → `track` (yaw / pitch assemblies rotate with finite rates - the same angles drive the visual nodes and the launch direction of the tube mouths) → `fire` (2-missile salvo when aligned, in range and with line of sight; salvos are globally staggered) → `cooldown` → `track`…; `dead` (burning pedestal). |
| **Boss** (`boss.ts`) | `entering` (slow descent) → `shielded` (shield sphere absorbs everything) ⇄ `vulnerable` (shield broken: hull / core takes damage; the shield comes back weaker after a while) → `dying` (chain explosions, victory). Attacks are a sub-machine: homing missile salvo, plasma volleys, shock-wave (when the player is close) and - once the hull drops below 35 % and the boss *enrages* - a tracking core beam with a visible charge-up. |
| **Wave director** (`waves.ts`) | `idle` → `intermission` → `active` → (`intermission` …) → `victory`; the boss wave keeps the escorts topped up. |

## Requirements

Node.js 20.19+ / 22+, a browser with WebGL2 (Chrome / Edge / Firefox). Blender 4.4 is only required for `npm run assets`.
Quality can be changed in the menus (Low / Medium / High); the game lowers it automatically if the frame rate stays low.
